$comment: Performance budgets. Baselines are first measurements; a check fails when a value regresses past its section's allowedRegression, and a section without a baseline is reported, not failed. openingFrameTime: just perf-opening (record with: just perf-opening record), headless Chromium since #48 (ADR 0144): its frames come on a 60 Hz clock, so p50 and p95 read 16.7 ms while the onboarding frame keeps up, against WebKit's 17 and 18. startup, idleMemory, inputLatency, freshDeskAtRest, deskOutOfSight: just perf-app on the CEF desk, nightly in the e2e workflow's perf job; their baselines come from the CI runner (just perf-app record, or budgets.json from the job's artifact), and none was recorded on the Tauri app, so the CEF desk's first run sets them. targetMs are RT-16's targets, printed beside the values, not gates. compose, composeStartup, surfaceStartup, surfaceMemory, inputToPaint, inputFromRest, deskAtRest: just perf-compositor (#58, e2e/perf/lib/compositor.ts) on the reference machine (docs/qa/TESTING.md); each section says why in its reason. budgetMs is a budget the value stays under, allowedRegression an allowance past a baseline, band a share either side of one; a baseline recorded on another platform or with another tool, and a budget on a software adapter, are reported, never failed.

compose.reason: #32 §3: composing 15 live surfaces at 1440p within 4 ms leaves 12 of a 60 Hz frame's 16.7 ms to the engine's paints and the shell. Gated on the p95 frame of cargo bench -p desk-compositor --bench compose (every window moved and every texture repainted each frame, so every frame is a full redraw; animate, compose and GPU done), on a GPU; a software adapter (lavapipe, WARP) reports it. p95Ms and medianMs are the reference machine's, kept for the trend.

composeStartup.reason: The compositor's own start, which every desk start waits for before it shows anything: from asking for a GPU device to the first composed frame of the compose budget's desk with the GPU done (device, pipelines, the machine's fonts, 15 textures uploaded, the first glyphs). The same bench run's median of three starts after one that warms what the OS and the driver keep for a new binary (a fresh build's first start took 4 times as long). Fails past the allowance on the platform its baseline was recorded on; the desk's whole start is surfaceStartup's.

surfaceStartup.reason: The desk's start to the first composed frame holding a web surface's paint, the median of ten starts in a row after one that takes the OS's first look at a newly laid out bundle (3.6 s against 0.2 s); the slowest of the ten is judged against the same baseline and allowance, so one stalled start fails, and is kept beside it (slowestMs). Until #112 two starts in five spent 1.4 s more before the desk's main ran, busy machine or quiet: Chromium's code-sign clone hard-linked the executable at every start, so macOS's exec policy took it for a new binary and scanned it again; the shell turns the clone off, and #58 had taken the fastest of five. Starts whose CEF took over a second are counted in stalls. The CEF desk in compositor mode through its surface probe (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs), started by the test, so the process's start, CEF's, a renderer's, the page's first paint, its import and a compose all count. #35 measured 137 to 248 ms from CreateBrowser to the first paint alone. Fails past the allowance on the platform its baseline was recorded on.

surfaceMemory.page: the PoC's light page, animating, 800x600 at scale 2, composed at 1920x1080
surfaceMemory.source: #35 (spikes/compositor/README.md): 916 MiB for the whole process tree with 1 light surface, 2,002 MiB with 10, so (2,002 - 916) / 9 a surface
surfaceMemory.reason: What one more live surface costs the machine, the number the live budget (ADR 0142: visible windows and the 8 most recent) is set from: the process tree's physical footprint with 1 and with 10 animating light surfaces, the difference per surface, as #35 measured it (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs). Within 20 % of #35's either way: above means a surface costs more than the live budget assumed; below means the baseline is stale or the surfaces did not render. RSS on Linux and Windows is reported until #61 records their baselines. Since #111 (ADR 0152) every surface renders on the desk's frame clock (external begin frames): 121.1 to 130 MiB a surface on the reference machine, where #52's internal begin frames read 162 to 191 (179.5 on main the same day), the GPU process holding about 60 MiB a surface more; on Chromium's full pipeline (#117, ADR 0157) 117.5 to 119.7. #35's baseline stays: this is the number the live budget was set from.

inputToPaint.reason: RT-16, input to screen within 16 ms, on the compositor's input path (#56): a press sent to a surface as the router sends it (pointer.down and pointer.up), twenty times beside two animating surfaces, through the surface probe (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs). Two gates: the press to the surface's next paint reaching the compositor, p95 (p95Ms, what the engine and the import cost), and to the desk's first composed frame holding it, median (frameP50Ms). The frame waits for the desk's own 60 Hz clock, so its p95 is the paint's plus up to a frame, 19 to 24 ms here, and is kept for the trend (frameP95Ms) rather than gated; RT-16's 16 ms at p95 would need a compose on damage, not on the clock. Since #111 (ADR 0152) a surface renders only on the desk's begin frames, and each step of a paint (the renderer's frame, the display's draw, the capture) waits for one: a press on an idle surface brings begin frames every 1 ms from the press until its paint. Since #117 (ADR 0157) Chromium runs its full pipeline, so a begin frame an idle page had nothing to draw for no longer holds the next ones back for a whole frame (CEF sends none while one is out), the one press in ten #111 saw wait a frame. The values are #117's median run of five at a load average of 5 to 8: the paint's p95 read 4.9 to 9.2 ms and the frame's median 13.5 to 14.7, where main read 9.4 to 14.2 and 15.2 to 15.8 in three runs the same hour (#111 read 12.1 to 22.3 and 13.9 to 17.9 on a busier machine). Since #129 (ADR 0159) five more presses are caught on purpose by CEF's busy-wait (a task delayed 5 ms after the press and CEF's work run at once, so that call loops out its 10 ms slice, as Chromium's own timers make one do now and then): gated, their paint's wait after the busy-wait ends, the median (caughtWaitMs within caughtWaitBudgetMs), since the frame clock's begin frames go out from a stand-in thread meanwhile and CEF's busy-wait runs them; kept for the trend, the press to that paint (caughtPaintP50Ms, at least the slice's 10 ms, as the desk's event loop waits for the call). #129's five runs at a load average of 8 to 13: the wait 0.01 to 0.04 ms (0.92 in a sixth run), the press to the paint 10.7 to 11.4; main's pump read 4.1 to 5.0 ms and 13.7 to 16.4 in the probe. The twenty presses read 5.3 to 12.2 ms at p95 (two of them caught by chance in the 12.2) and 13.0 to 15.5 at the frame's median.

inputFromRest.reason: #133 (ADR 0162): RT-16 on a desk at rest, through the surface probe's idle-input run (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs): three still surfaces, two of them the click page, pressed in turn twelve times, each press after the desk rested 2, 2.5 or 3 s (the probe's loop run as the window's at rest), so every pressed surface is long idle on the slow clock (ADR 0157) and nothing on the desk has painted for seconds. Gated: the press to its paint reaching the compositor, p95 (the second slowest of twelve), within budgetMs. Kept for the trend: the median, the slowest, and the composed frame's median, which waits for the desk's next frame (16.7 ms after the press: the desk composed nothing at rest). After a second or more with nothing painted the GPU sleeps, and the first copy after (Chromium's capture in its GPU process, the desk's attach in its own) took 3 to 12 ms to finish where a busy desk's takes a fraction of one; neither the slow clock, the renderer nor CEF's pump was the wait. Main painted 10.0 to 16.9 ms after the press at the median and 10.2 to 23.3 at p95 in six runs at a load average of 2.5 to 6, over the budget in four; with input to a cold desk waking the GPU's copies at once (apps/desk/shell/src/web_host/copy_wake.rs) 8.3 to 14.7 and 12.9 to 16.1 in nine runs, within it in eight (16.07 once, at a load average of 2.5). Its floor is the GPU's own wake-up, which starts at the press: a copy of a few pixels took 4 to 13 ms to finish on a quiet machine. #148: the machine's cores set the rest of the floor. The gate read 8.0 to 8.4 ms in #134's runs and 15.1 to 21.6 later the same day; run by run, presses painted 5.8 to 15.8 ms after them on a quiet machine and 6.5 to 7.8 with one busy loop anywhere on it, and a core kept busy by the desk from the press on did not help. So the run presses once first, not counted, then three blocks of twelve (blocks, warmUp), and the gate reads the block whose p95 is the median (blockP95Ms keeps all three): a burst of other work during one block, or its end, does not decide a run. Five runs at a load average of 3.9 to 7.3: 12.69 to 13.21 ms (blocks 12.41 to 14.92). The values are the median run of the five; tries counts the median block's presses.

deskAtRest.reason: #129 (ADR 0159), #134 (ADR 0164): what a desk at rest costs, through the surface probe's rest run (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs): three still surfaces, shown and awake, each long idle, which since #134 take no begin frames, and the probe's loop run for ten seconds as the compositor window's event loop runs (a turn, then a wait for CEF's next work, the clock's next look or CEF's ask). Gated: the loop's wake-ups a second (each turn of the event loop) within wakeupsBudget, where main's pump woke 54.6 to 57.7 times (its poll every 33 ms whatever the clock did), #129's 33.2 to 38.3 (CEF's answers to the slow clock's ten begin frames a second a surface) and #134's 10.1 to 10.3 (CEF's poll every 100 ms, ADR 0159); the browser process's CPU within cpuBudgetPercent of a core (0.5 to 0.7 %); and after the rest a fourth page that changes itself by a timer, three times, each once it is long idle: from each change to its paint, the median within ownChangeBudgetMs (49.6 to 51.6 ms: its page asks for frames, frame_asks.js; the slow clock read 107). Kept for the trend: the browser process's OS wake-ups (macOS proc_pid_rusage: 30.6 to 30.7 a second, CEF's own threads), CEF's work calls a second, the begin frames a second (none) and the slowest own change; a press from rest is inputFromRest's since #133. The values are #134's median run of five at a load average of 5 to 8.

freshDeskAtRest.reason: #134 (ADR 0164): a fresh desk left alone, through just perf-app (e2e/perf/rest.perf.ts): the Default profile with its first run, gone through as a person in a hurry does (Skip for now, Later, Not now, a name, the first suggested task), then twenty seconds alone and ten measured with ps: the app's own process's CPU as a share of one core, within budgetPercent, a budget that fails from the first run (no baseline needed), and its whole tree's kept beside it. Before #134 it read 59.2 % (its tree 124.9 %): the first run's animation, Eris's idle motion drawn on a canvas at every frame in the shell page and in her floating window, the runtime's ticker and the page's report asking for a frame at every frame, messages waking every surface for a second, and on the reference machine's locked screen the compositor composing at every desk frame for a window that withheld its frames. After: 3.1 to 3.4 % in three runs at a load average of 5 to 9 (its tree 5.3 to 5.7 %). On 2026-11-11 the same head read 6.6 to 6.8 % at a load average of 4 to 5: the palette, never summoned, took Chromium's 60 Hz begin frames in its page and its frame, the desk's own process answering each. Since #147 a hidden floating window's page is hidden (apps/desk/shell/src/pane.rs): 2.8, 2.8, 3.0 and 3.2 % in four runs in a row at a load average of 3.8 to 5.5 (its tree 3.8 to 4.8 %), against 3.6 and 6.1 % (5.9 and 11.6 %) without it the same hour. Left: on the e2e desk Eris floats (the desk is not the app in front) and her window takes Chromium's 60 Hz begin frames with an idle page; CEF's busy-wait (ADR 0159) about twice a second for a delayed task of Chromium's own; endue.docker's proc.spawn every few seconds. The values are the median run of the four (#147's).

deskOutOfSight.reason: #155: a desk nobody can see, through just perf-app (e2e/perf/hidden.perf.ts): the main window closed with its red button, then minimized, each ten seconds measured once three have passed (the spin started within about 3 s), then brought back as the Dock icon does it. Gated, each the worse of the two: the app's own process's CPU as a share of one core within budgetPercent, freshDeskAtRest's budget for a desk in sight; the event loop's turns a second (compositor_stats' pump.turns) within turnsBudget, under a visible desk's 24 to 78 at rest; and from the window brought back to its first composed frame within shownBudgetMs. All three are budgets, failing from the first run. Before #155 the main process spun at 99 to 100 % and 14,000 to 19,000 turns a second for as long as the window was out of sight, closed, minimized, hidden, covered or on another Space: the frame clock named a frame due at the last one's time, long past, and the loop never waited. Where the OS says nothing of a window out of sight (a locked screen; X11 without a window manager) the spec feeds the event winit hands the shell itself (compositor_window { occluded }) and keeps told: false beside the values: the wait it checks is the desk's own. On the reference machine with its screen locked (the OS said nothing, so the spec fed it), a debug build on a machine busy with other work: 1.3 to 1.4 % and 29 to 38 turns a second out of sight with the driver attached (16 to 22 without it), the frame 35 to 48 ms after the window came back; the same run on the old frame rule failed at 100.3 % and 42,581 turns a second.
